title: Eco-Safe Driving & the Environment
whatItIs: Eco-safe driving means planning ahead and driving smoothly, avoiding unnecessary acceleration and braking. It saves fuel and cuts CO2.
keyFacts: Plan ahead so you can avoid harsh braking and sudden acceleration.
Change up through the gears early, usually by about 2,000 rpm.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT leave your engine running unnecessarily while stopped on a public road.

keyFacts: Remove roof boxes when not needed: at motorway speeds one can raise fuel use by around 25%.
Under-inflated tyres and extra weight make the car use more fuel.
Fuel use rises with speed: at 70 mph a car uses about 10% more fuel than at 60 mph.

items.title: Look well ahead
items.text: Ease off early instead of braking hard at the last moment.

items.title: Smooth and steady
items.text: Gentle acceleration and a steady speed use the least fuel.

items.title: Engine off when parked
items.text: Don't leave it running unnecessarily while stationary on a public road.

items.title: Travel light
items.text: Remove roof boxes and unneeded weight. Keep tyres inflated.

b.label: Coasting
points: Rolling in neutral or with the clutch down

onTheTest.question: How can you reduce your fuel consumption?
options: Plan ahead and avoid harsh braking
Accelerate hard to reach your cruising speed
Keep the engine running when parked
Stay in lower gears for longer
onTheTest.why: Planning ahead lets you ease off early instead of braking hard, which saves fuel and is safer.

traps: Coasting reduces your control: engine braking is lost and speed builds quickly downhill.
Leaving the engine running while parked can be an offence, not just a waste.
A roof box left on when empty still costs you fuel.
